The UK's 2027 Jaecoo 7 Luxury+ PHEV Adds 349-HP AWD Option
7 photos
Photo: Jaecoo / edited
Controlled by Chinese automaker Chery, the Jaecoo brand has expanded the 7 range for the United Kingdom with two Luxury+ configurations. Officially dubbed 7 SHS-P Luxury+, this fellow has a few things going for it, beginning with optional AWD and a larger battery. 349 ponies are on the menu in AWD flavor, and revised driver assistance software also needs highlighting.
Starting with the ADAS part, British media recently put the Hybrid Pure to the test. It recorded six false driver monitoring alerts and two false lane departure warnings on the test route, which is why the Jaecoo finished sixth out of seven participants. Criticized for its sensitivity, the advanced driver assistance suite promises to be less intrusive in the Luxury+.
A new one-touch setting lets British customers apply their preferred assistance configuration without digging through multiple digital menus via the central touchscreen. If you ask me, that's a sensible change to prioritize for the new model year. After all, any type of active automotive safety equipment should make driving easier rather than hinder the experience.
The revised ADAS software is debuting in the Luxury+, yes, but the rest of the 7 will get it from early 2027. Having cleared that up, the plug-in hybrid version of the Super Hybrid System is finally available with all-wheel drive. This powertrain is rated at 354 ps (349 hp), with peak torque estimated at 490 Nm (361 lb-ft).
In optimal conditions, the Luxury+ PHEV AWD needs 5.9 seconds to hit 62 miles per hour (100 kilometers per hour). On paper, that's quite a jump from the 7.9 seconds of the front-drive model. Rated at 204 ps (201 hp) and 365 Nm (269 lb-ft) of twist, said version takes 7.9 seconds and costs £1,500 less.
Photo: Jaecoo The Luxury+ plug-in hybrid with all-wheel drive comes with the usual compromise, namely less electric range than its front-wheel-drive sibling. Jaecoo estimates 70 miles (113 kilometers) on a full charge as opposed to 79 miles (127 kilometers) with front-wheel drive, and that's all due to the additional weight of the electrified rear axle.
In the Luxury+, the high-voltage battery has been upgraded from the former 18.4 kilowatt-hours to 26.6 kilowatt-hours, marking an increase of approximately 45 percent. Jaecoo says the upgrade adds up to 23 miles of electric-only range compared to the current plug-in hybrid system. For customers who do most of their driving around town, said extra capacity will come in handy.
DC fast charging also gets upgraded to 65 kilowatts, with Jaecoo quoting 15 minutes from 30 to 80 percent state of charge. Under the hood, both the front- and all-wheel-drive PHEVs feature a 1.5-liter turbocharged inline-four mill. Beyond pure-electric driving, both switch between series- and parallel-hybrid operation.
The 1.5 underhood is claimed to deliver 44.5 percent thermal efficiency, which is a lot. By comparison, Toyota often claims 40 and 41 percent nowadays for its 2.5- and 1.5-liter hybrid mills. Jaecoo 7 customers who are wondering if the Luxury+ with all-wheel drive can hold its own in off-pavement scenarios will be happy to learn that 183 millimeters (7.2 inches) of ground clearance is the norm.
The approach and departure angles are listed as 20.5 and 28.5 degrees, respectively. While said figures don't threaten the Jeep Wrangler Rubicon, they're good enough for the occasional venture off the beaten path.
As of this writing, Jaecoo's British division lists the 7 SHS-P Luxury+ at £37,000 with front-wheel drive or £38,500 for the all-wheel-drive version. Both are covered by a seven-year vehicle warranty and eight years for the high-voltage battery.
